variables.title: Variables & Constants
variables.code:
# Variables are dynamically typed
x = 10
name = "Alice"

# Python doesn't have a const keyword
# By convention, constants are ALL_CAPS
MAX_CONNECTIONS = 100

# Type hints (Python 3.5+)
from typing import Final
PI: Final = 3.14159
variables.notes: Python is dynamically typed. It has no strict constants at the language level, but naming conventions and typing.Final indicate intent.

data_types.title: Data Types
data_types.code:
# Primitives
i = 42          # int
f = 3.14        # float
b = True        # bool
s = "Hello"     # str

# Collections
l = [1, 2, 3]   # list
d = {'a': 1}    # dict
t = (1, 2)      # tuple
set_val = {1}   # set
data_types.notes: Python automatically infers types. Collections are highly flexible and can hold mixed types.

operators.title: Operators
operators.code:
# Arithmetic
sum = 10 + 5
div = 10 / 3      # Float division (3.333...)
floor_div = 10 // 3 # Integer division (3)
mod = 10 % 3
pow = 2 ** 3      # Exponentiation

# Logical
is_true = True and False
is_or = True or False
is_not = not True
operators.notes: Uses words ('and', 'or', 'not') for logical operators instead of symbols like '&&' or '||'.

conditionals.title: Conditionals
conditionals.notes: Python relies on indentation rather than braces for conditional blocks.

for_loop.title: For Loop
for_loop.notes: The 'for' loop in Python acts strictly as an iterator over sequences or iterables.

while_loop.title: While Loop
while_loop.notes: Python's while loop supports an 'else' clause that runs if the loop terminates normally.

functions.title: Functions
functions.code:
# Basic function with type hints
def greet(name: str) -> str:
    return f"Hello, {name}!"

# Default parameters and keyword arguments
def power(base: int, exp: int = 2) -> int:
    return base ** exp

result = power(3)
res2 = power(exp=3, base=2)
functions.notes: Functions are first-class objects. Type hints are optional but highly recommended.

arrays.title: Arrays / Lists
arrays.code:
numbers = [1, 2, 3]

# Append & modify
numbers.append(4)
numbers[0] = 99

# Slicing [start:stop:step]
subset = numbers[1:3] # [2, 3]

# List comprehension (idiomatic)
squares = [x**2 for x in numbers if x > 0]
arrays.notes: Python lists are dynamic arrays. List comprehensions offer a concise way to create lists.

maps.title: Maps / Dictionaries
maps.code:
user = {
    "name": "Alice",
    "age": 30
}

# Add/update
user["role"] = "admin"

# Safe access
age = user.get("age", 0)

# Iteration
for key, value in user.items():
    print(f"{key}: {value}")
maps.notes: Dictionaries in Python are insertion-ordered (since 3.7) and highly optimized.

error_handling.title: Error Handling
error_handling.notes: Python uses try/except blocks. It encourages a 'Look before you leap' or 'Easier to ask forgiveness' approach.

comments.title: Comments & Documentation
comments.code:
# Single-line comment in Python

"""
Multi-line documentation block.
Provides docstrings for functions and modules.
"""

def add(a, b):
    """Return sum of a and b."""
    return a + b
comments.notes: Python uses # for line comments and triple quotes for multi-line documentation strings.

numbers.title: Numbers & Numerics
numbers.notes: Python supports arbitrary-precision or native integers, IEEE floats, and numeric literal prefixes (0x, 0b).

booleans.title: Booleans & Conditions
booleans.code:
is_active = True
has_failed = False

if is_active and not has_failed:
    print("Active")
booleans.notes: Python represents boolean values with logical and, or, and not operators.

type_casting.title: Type Casting & Conversion
type_casting.code:
num_str = "42"
n = int(num_str)
f = float(n)
s = str(f)
type_casting.notes: Python uses explicit conversion functions or operators to transform types between primitives.

strings.title: Strings & Escapes
strings.code:
s1 = "Double-quoted string"
s2 = 'Single-quoted string'
raw = r"C:\new_folder\raw.txt"
multi = """Line 1
Line 2"""
strings.notes: Python supports single, double, and raw string literals that ignore escape characters.

string_formatting.title: String Formatting
string_formatting.code:
name = "Alice"
score = 95
msg = f"User {name} scored {score:.1f}"
print(msg)
string_formatting.notes: Python uses f-string interpolation or format specifiers for embedded expression formatting.

pattern_matching.title: Pattern Matching
pattern_matching.code:
match val:
    case 1:
        print("One")
    case 2 | 3:
        print("Two or Three")
    case _:
        print("Default")
pattern_matching.notes: Python provides structural pattern matching with match/case or case-of expressions.

range.title: Ranges & Slices
range.code:
r = range(1, 10, 2)
sub = nums[1:5]
rev = nums[::-1]
range.notes: Python provides built-in range generation and slicing syntax with interval boundaries.

iterators.title: Iterators & Generators
iterators.notes: Python uses generator functions or iterators with the yield keyword for lazy element production.

oop_classes.title: Classes & OOP
oop_classes.notes: Python supports object-oriented paradigms with methods, constructors, and encapsulation.

lists.title: Lists & Dynamic Arrays
lists.notes: Python provides mutable dynamic lists/sequences with append, insert, and indexing operations.

tuples.title: Tuples & Records
tuples.notes: Python provides immutable ordered tuples supporting unpack destructuring.

sets.title: Sets & Collections
sets.notes: Python provides unique element set collections with membership tests and mathematical set operations.

modules_import.title: Modules & Imports
modules_import.code:
import math
from math import sqrt, pi
import os.path as path
modules_import.notes: Python manages code organization via modules and selective import statements.
